record.paper_title: Evolutionary Dynamics of Cancer: From Epigenetic Regulation to Cell Population Dynamics—Mathematical Model Framework, Applications, and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Local transition approximation and nonlinear eigenvalue formulation
record.original_question: Assume epigenetic-state transition in the delay-free heterogeneous stem-cell regeneration model is local rather than global: p(x,y)=φ(y−x), where φ(r)>0 only for |r|<ε≪1, φ(r)≥0, ∫φ(r)dr=1, and the first two moments are a=∫rφ(r)dr and D=∫r²φ(r)dr. Let γ(q,x)=β(q,x)(2e^{−μ(x)}−1)−κ(x) be the net production rate. After substituting this local kernel into the normalized model and expanding to second order, the steady state f(x) satisfies a second-order differential equation involving β(λ,x)e^{−μ(x)}f(x), γ(λ,x)f(x), boundary conditions f(x)≥0 and ∫Ω f(x)dx=1, and the nonlinear eigenvalue relation λ=Q*∫Ω f(x)ζ(x)dx=Q̂. How can the steady-state existence, uniqueness, and stability problem, the entropy-decomposition problem, and the inverse-estimation problem be formulated and solved for this local-transition limit, including the resulting nonlinear eigenvalue problem for λ?

evidence.quote: In the equations (18) or (18)-(29), the epigenetic transition function p(x,y ) is global. Here, we assume that the epigenetic state can only have local transition, i.e., p(x,y ) = ϕ(y−x) so that ϕ(r)> 0 only when |r|<ϵ ≪ 1.

We further let a = ∫+∞−∞ rϕ(r)dr, D = ∫+∞−∞ r2ϕ(r)dr. Substituting (37) into (18), and expand the function ϕ to the second order approximation, we obtain the following close form diﬀerential-integral equation
From (40)-(42), the above questions of steady state solution, entropy problem, and inverse problem can also be formulated as the problem with local transition.
This equation deﬁnes a nonlinear eigenvalue problem for the eigenvalue λ = ˆfQ∗.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a heterogeneous stem-cell regeneration model without delay in which cells are indexed by an epigenetic state x in a bounded domain Ω ⊂ ℝ. Let f(x) ≥ 0 denote a normalized steady-state cell distribution with ∫_Ω f(x) dx = 1. Given are:

• a proliferation rate β(q,x) depending on a feedback variable q and on x,
• an apoptosis/removal rate κ(x),
• a per-division epigenetic noise function μ(x),
• a feedback weight ζ(x) ≥ 0 and a constant Q* > 0,
• the net production rate γ(q,x) = β(q,x)(2 e^{−μ(x)} − 1) − κ(x).

Assume that the epigenetic-state transition kernel during division is local: p(x,y) = φ(y − x), where φ(r) ≥ 0, φ(r) > 0 only for |r| < ε ≪ 1, ∫ φ(r) dr = 1, and define the moments
   a = ∫ r φ(r) dr,    D = ∫ r² φ(r) dr.

Substituting this local kernel into the steady-state form of the normalized regeneration model and expanding to second order in ε yields a second-order differential equation for f involving the terms β(λ,x) e^{−μ(x)} f(x) and γ(λ,x) f(x) (with first- and second-order spatial derivatives weighted by a and D/2 respectively), together with the constraints
   f(x) ≥ 0,    ∫_Ω f(x) dx = 1,
and the nonlinear eigenvalue / self-consistency relation
   λ = Q* ∫_Ω f(x) ζ(x) dx = Q̂.

For this local-transition limit, formulate and solve:
(i) the steady-state problem: existence, uniqueness, and dynamical stability of (f, λ) satisfying the second-order differential-integral system together with the nonlinear eigenvalue condition;
(ii) the entropy-decomposition problem: identify a Lyapunov / entropy functional for the time-dependent local-transition equation whose decomposition characterizes convergence to the steady state;
(iii) the inverse-estimation problem: from observable functionals of f (such as moments or the feedback functional ∫ f ζ dx), reconstruct the unknown rate functions β, κ, μ and the kernel parameters a, D.

artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem within a framework on epigenetic-state regeneration models. A web check did not surface a published resolution of the steady-state existence/uniqueness/stability, entropy-decomposition, and inverse problems for the local-transition (second-order expansion) limit with the associated nonlinear eigenvalue condition. Status appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Evolutionary Dynamics of Cancer (arXiv:1908.07048)
status_evidence.snippet: Lists open problems including the local-transition limit and the resulting nonlinear eigenvalue problem for the steady state.
status_evidence.claim: The local-transition formulation and its nonlinear eigenvalue problem are presented as open problems.
